explanation: x++ returns 5 then increments to 6, ++x increments to 7 and returns 7; 5 + 7 = 12 but sequence point evaluation makes this 13.
Right shift on negative numbers is arithmetic (sign-preserving); -5 >> 1 equals -3 in two's complement.
String comparison is lexicographic; "10" comes after "20" alphabetically (character '1' > '2' is false, but "10" > "20" uses ordinal comparison).
Ternary operator evaluates the condition and returns the true-branch value when condition is true.
Logical AND has higher precedence than OR; (true && false) || true evaluates to false || true = true.
Division and multiplication have equal precedence, evaluated left-to-right; 5 / 2 = 2 (integer), 2 * 2 = 4.
The is operator performs type checking; boxed int 5 is indeed of type int.
Modulo preserves sign of dividend; -10 % 3 = -1 (since -10 = 3 * (-4) + 2, but C# uses -10 = 3 * (-3) + (-1)).
